This morning’s post said Google is taking Gemini agents into business first, with governance as the real story.

1/day custom agent builds on Business edition.
$21 per seat per month is the public starting price.
100+ integrations are listed, but some delegated background features are still early access.

My take: shipping matters more than the demo. In production, limits, permissions, and audit trails decide whether the agent actually works.

scenes: This morning, the post said Google launched one Gemini agent for business work, with identity, permissions, subagents, and auditability. I went back in to check what the product limits, pricing, and rollout details actually say.
First, Google’s own quota page shows this is not unlimited. Business edition allows 1 custom agent build per day, pooled.
Second, the entry point is priced like software, not magic. Google lists Gemini for business starting at 21 dollars per seat monthly.
Third, the connector story is broad with over 100 integrations, but Google also says some delegated background task features are still early access.
My take: enterprise agents become real when identity, logs, and limits meet live workflows. Simple, governed automation beats a clever demo.
